### `stability`

### `fock_reproducible`

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | boolean |
| Default | `False` |
| Used by | every two-electron Fock build (SCF, TDHF/TDDFT/MRSF response, z-vector) |

By default the two-electron Fock build hands shell pairs to OpenMP threads
dynamically, so the order in which contributions are summed, and hence the
last bits of the Fock matrix, changes from run to run. Two calculations of the
same input then stop at SCF points that differ slightly (orbitals by about
1e-9 at `conv=1e-8`). Energies are unaffected at any meaningful precision,
but quantities that are not stationary in the orbitals, and nearly degenerate
SCF solutions, can differ in the last digits between runs.

With `fock_reproducible=true` each shell pair is assigned to a fixed thread,
every thread accumulates its own Fock copy, and the copies are summed in
thread order. Repeated runs with the same `OMP_NUM_THREADS` and the same MPI
rank count then give bitwise identical energies and orbitals; the XC build is
always reproducible in this sense. Different thread counts still differ in
the last bits. The option costs about 2-4 % of the two-electron Fock time and
always keeps one Fock copy per thread (the low-memory shared atomic Fock is
not used).

```text
rks/b3lypv5/6-31g* scf(fock_reproducible=true)
```

### `fock_reproducible`

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | boolean |
| Default | `False` |
| Used by | native CPU Fock and selected XC, response, and gradient builders |

Set `scf(fock_reproducible=true)` to use fixed OpenMP work assignments
and a fixed accumulation order in the supported native builders. The
two-electron Fock build keeps one private Fock matrix per thread.
Fixed-order accumulation rejects multiple MPI ranks, GPU-linked builds,
external providers, and atomic shared-Fock accumulation where these
would conflict with the selected path.

Keep the same binary, inputs, initial electronic state, and OpenMP and
BLAS thread counts when comparing runs. Reproducible accumulation does
not guarantee bitwise agreement of a whole calculation. The NAMD check
covers one gas-phase MRSF/BHHLYP ethylene case with an explicit Hückel
guess, finite-difference couplings, and isotropic velocity rescaling.
See [the verified ethylene restart procedure](../result-files.md#ethylene-restart-example)
and [its downloadable .oqp input](../ethylene-namd-restart.oqp).

Use `json` for exact restarts and `auto` for workflows that may or may not have
a previous restart file.

Use `guess(type=huckel)` to reproduce a run started from extended Hückel. An explicit fresh guess such as `huckel`, `minao`, or `sap` does not read saved orbitals. Explicit `minao` rejects atoms beyond Cm. For an effective core potential, MINAO removes the replaced core density before projection. SAP caps the tabulated effective charge at the valence nuclear charge and includes the ECP operator.

Use `guess(type=json,file="previous.npz")` when an orbital restart is required. Save converged orbitals with `guess(save_mol=true)`, keep the original result, and reconverge the target calculation.

When no file is specified, the default `auto` guess looks for the result
beside the input, such as `water.npz` or `water.json` for `water.oqp`. If both exist, automatic
discovery selects a standalone NPZ and records that choice in the log.
OpenQP checks SCF convergence and compatibility before restoring orbitals.
The input geometry remains authoritative by default. An explicit fresh
guess such as `guess(type=minao)` bypasses restart discovery.

Specify the full result filename, as in `guess(file="previous.npz")`. With no path, `auto` computes the fresh guess described above. An existing invalid result raises an error during loading. The input geometry remains authoritative unless a supported explicit restart requests the saved geometry.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Type | boolean |
| Default | `False` |

Use `guess(occupation_trials=true)` to compare candidate occupations when an
initial guess has a degenerate orbital level at an occupation boundary that
splits into different symmetry components. Each candidate gets up to five SCF
iterations. The main SCF starts from the orbitals and density of the candidate
with the lowest trial energy. This short comparison does not establish the
lowest fully converged SCF state.

OpenQP skips the trials when the occupation is selected by MO swaps, MOM, or
restricted orbital rotation, when the candidate count exceeds the internal
limit, or when the calculation uses QM/MM embedding. By default the orbital
symmetry adaptation uses the symmetry table order without running trials.


The `occupation_trials` control is unavailable in this 1.4 engine.
